section_summary.extract_value: This section (3.3.1) presents results from multilevel analyses examining the relationship between exposure to body-focused and non-body-focused others and intuitive eating. At the between-persons level, greater mean exposure to non-body-focused others positively predicted intuitive eating, while greater exposure to body-focused others negatively predicted it. At the within-persons level, daily exposure to non-body-focused others showed a trend toward predicting intuitive eating, and preceding changes in such exposure significantly predicted intuitive eating. Additionally, changes in intuitive eating predicted subsequent exposure to non-body-focused others, suggesting bidirectional relationships.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents results from multilevel models examining predictors of intuitive eating, dietary restraint, body appreciation, and body satisfaction. At the between-persons level, exposure to non-body focused others positively predicted intuitive eating while exposure to body-focused others negatively predicted it. At the within-persons level, daily deviations in exposure to non-body focused others positively predicted intuitive eating. The text also reports bidirectional relationships, showing that changes in intuitive eating predicted subsequent exposure to non-body focused others. Table 2 displays fixed effects coefficients, standard errors, F-statistics, and degrees of freedom for all four outcome variables.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents results from multilevel models predicting intuitive eating, dietary restraint, body appreciation, and body satisfaction based on daily changes in exposure to body-focused and non-body-focused others. Table 3 displays fixed effects coefficients showing that BMI negatively predicted body appreciation (β = -0.34), and that preceding changes in non-body-focused exposure positively predicted intuitive eating and body appreciation, while body-focused exposure showed minimal effects. The study appears to be a single longitudinal experience sampling study examining within-person and between-person associations.
